entities.name: PMID:19996800
observations: Long-term reassessment of 637 comparable polytrauma survivors at a mean of 17 years after injury; men and women had similar injury severity.

Women had higher PTSD prevalence than men (14.5% vs 6.2%, p=0.035), more psychological support/treatment (28.0% vs 15.0%, p<0.001), longer rehabilitation and sick leave, and lower psychological quality-of-life scores.
The proportion feeling well rehabilitated was similar between women and men (75.3% vs 75.4%).

entities.name: Male quality of life
observations: Compared with premenopausal women after comparable polytrauma, men had higher psychological quality-of-life scores at long-term follow-up.
This finding is the closest direct match among the answer choices because women, rather than men, had more PTSD and psychiatric treatment.

entities.name: Female PTSD after polytrauma
observations: At mean 17-year follow-up after comparable polytrauma, PTSD was more frequent in women than men: 14.5% versus 6.2%, p=0.035.
